The set of vectors $\{ \mathbf{v}_1, \mathbf{v}_2, \ldots, \mathbf{v}_n \}$ in an abstract vector space $V$ is **linearly dependent** if there exist real scalars $x_1,x_2,\ldots,x_n$ not all zero such that 

$$
x_1\mathbf{v}_1+x_2\mathbf{v}_2+\ldots+x_n\mathbf{v}_n=\mathbf{0}.
$$

Otherwise, if $x_1 = x_2 = \cdots = x_n = 0$ is the only solution, the set is **linearly independent**.

Let's consider some examples.

- First, let's consider the vector space $\mathbb{R}[t]$ of all polynomials in variable $t,$ along with the set

$$
S = \big\{ \underbrace{1}_{\color{blue}p_1(t)}, \: \underbrace{t}_{\color{blue}p_2(t)}, \: \underbrace{t^2}_{\color{blue}p_3(t)} \big\}.
$$

To determine whether $S$ is linearly dependent in $\mathbb{R}[t],$ we must solve the equation

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}{\color{blue}{p}_{1}(t)}+{x}_{2}{\color{blue}{p}_{2}(t)}+{x}_{3}{\color{blue}{p}_{3}(t)} & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the given expressions for $p_1(t),p_2(t)$ and $p_3(t)$ into the above equation, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}\cdot 1+{x}_{2}\cdot t+{x}_{3}\cdot {t}^{2} & =0 \\ {x}_{1}+{x}_{2}t+{x}_{3}{t}^{2} & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

The final equation is true for every $t$ if and only if 

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} &=0 \\ {x}_{2} &=0 \\ {x}_{3} &=0.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Since $x_1 = x_2 = x_3 = 0$ is the only solution, $S$ is linearly independent in $\mathbb R[t].$

- Let's consider the vector space $\mathbb R[t]$ once more, along with the set 

$$
T = \big\{ \underbrace{t^2+1}_{\color{red}q_1(t)}, \: \underbrace{-2t^2-2}_{\color{red}q_2(t)} \big\}.
$$

To determine whether $T$ is linearly dependent in $\mathbb{R}[t],$ we must solve the equation

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}{\color{red}{q}_{1}(t)}+{x}_{2}{\color{red}{q}_{2}(t)} & =0 \\ {x}_{1}({t}^{2}+1)+{x}_{2}(-2{t}^{2}-2) & =0 \\ ({x}_{1}-2{x}_{2})+({x}_{1}-2{x}_{2}){t}^{2} & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

The final equation is true for every $t$ if and only if 

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-2{x}_{2} &=0 \\ {x}_{1}-2{x}_{2} &=0.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

This system has the nonzero solution $(x_1,x_2)=(2,1).$ As a result, we get

$$
2 \cdot {\color{red}q_1(t)} + 1 \cdot {\color{red}q_2(t)} = 0.
$$

Therefore, the set $\big\{ q_1(t), q_2(t) \big\}$ is linearly dependent in $\mathbb R[t].$

Note the following important property of linearly dependent sets.

*A set of vectors is linearly dependent if and only if it contains a vector that is a linear combination of **other** vectors from that set.*

To see why this is true, let $\{ \mathbf{v}_1, \mathbf{v}_2,\cdots, \mathbf{v}_n\}$ be a linearly dependent set of $n$ vectors. This means that the equation

$$
x_1\mathbf{v}_1 + x_2 \mathbf{v}_2 + \cdots + x_n\mathbf{v}_n = \mathbf{0}
$$

has a non-trivial solution, i.e. a solution in which at least one of the coefficients $x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n$ is not zero. Without loss of generality, we may assume that $x_1 \ne 0,$ and we can rewrite the above equation as

$$
\mathbf{v}_1 = -\dfrac{x_2}{x_1} \mathbf{v}_2 - \dfrac{x_3}{x_1}\mathbf{v}_3 - \cdots - \dfrac{x_n}{x_1}\mathbf{v}_n.
$$

The above argument shows that the vector $\mathbf{v}_1$ can be written as a linear combination of the other vectors from the set.

Consider a vector space $V$ and vectors ${v}_{1},{v}_{2},{v}_{3}\in V.$ Given that ${{v}_{1},{v}_{2},{v}_{3}}$ is linearly independent, which of the following statements are true?

Select all that apply.

Let's examine each of the given options in turn.

- Statement “${{v}_{1}+{v}_{2},{v}_{2}+{v}_{3},{v}_{3}}$ is linearly independent” is true. Suppose that

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}({v}_{1}+{v}_{2})+{x}_{2}({v}_{2}+{v}_{3})+{x}_{3}{v}_{3} & =0,\end{aligned}
$$

which, in turn, gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}{v}_{1}+({x}_{1}+{x}_{2}){v}_{2}+({x}_{2}+{x}_{3}){v}_{3} & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Since ${{v}_{1},{v}_{2},{v}_{3}}$ is a linearly independent set, the final equation can be true only if

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} &=0 \\ {x}_{1}+{x}_{2} &=0 \\ {x}_{2}+{x}_{3} &=0.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

The unique solution of the system is ${x}_{1}={x}_{2}={x}_{3}=0,$ which means that 

$$
{{v}_{1}+{v}_{2},{v}_{2}+{v}_{3},{v}_{3}}
$$

 is linearly independent.

- Statement “${0,{v}_{1},2{v}_{2}}$ is linearly independent” is false. Indeed, notice that

$$
1\cdot 0+0\cdot {v}_{1}+0\cdot (2{v}_{2})=0.
$$

As a result, ${x}_{1}0+{x}_{2}{v}_{1}+{x}_{3}(2{v}_{2})=0$ has a non-zero solution. This means that ${0,{v}_{1},2{v}_{2}}$ is linearly dependent. In general, any set containing the zero vector is linearly dependent.

- Statement “${{v}_{1},{v}_{2}}$ is linearly independent” is true. Indeed, ${x}_{1}{v}_{1}+{x}_{2}{v}_{2}=0$ must have only the zero solution ${x}_{1}={x}_{2}=0.$  If this equation has a non-zero solution, $a\cdot {v}_{1}+b\cdot {v}_{2}=0,$ then we obtain

$$
a\cdot {v}_{1}+b\cdot {v}_{2}+0\cdot {v}_{3}=0,
$$

which would mean that ${{v}_{1},{v}_{2},{v}_{3}}$ is linearly dependent.

Therefore, the correct answer is “${{v}_{1}+{v}_{2},{v}_{2}+{v}_{3},{v}_{3}}$ is linearly independent”; “${{v}_{1},{v}_{2}}$ is linearly independent” only.

Consider the set $\{{p}_{1}(t),{p}_{2}(t)\}$ of polynomials from $\mathbb{R}[t],$ where

$$

$$

$$

$$

$$

Now, we consider the corresponding augmented matrix and reduce it to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination:

$$

$$

$$

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-4{x}_{2}-3{x}_{3} &=0 \\ {x}_{1}-2{x}_{2}-2{x}_{3} &=0.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

$$

$$

$$

$$

$$
